about: An underground-empire cave adventure. You are a returning adventurer being tested by a silver-haired old man. There is a cliff with a locked chest and a taunting man above it, a secret stair behind a carved wall, an icy lake, and grues in the dark.

done.why: I carried the lantern into the lake and it was ruined for good. Every dark room kills me on the second step, so I could not get past the first rooms again. I gave up.

moments.note: The cliff man appears and mocks me from above, and the rope twitches. The world felt inhabited.
Giving bread to the old man opened a secret door. The stairs beyond turned me back, saying I was not yet ready.
Entering the lake dropped everything, and the lantern was ruined. This soft-locked me, and the warning was only a hint.
I died repeatedly in the dark and respawned with a dead lantern, with no way to recover.

wished: Some way to dry or replace the lantern.
A clearer warning that the lake would destroy the lamp.
To get the chest open, find the key, and see the south passage.

lines.line: The way down is not yours today. You come back up.
lines.why: It tells you there is more to gather before the finale.

lines.line: Your lamp goes under with the rest. There is a hiss, a brief glow in the water below you, and then not.
lines.why: This is where the game became unwinnable for me.

fun.why: The early exploration was good. The soft-lock ended it.

engagement.why: I was curious about the cliff man and the secret stair, but I got cut off from them.

difficulty.why: One mistake ruined the lamp and left no recovery.

interestingness.why: The world has reactive details such as the taunting man and the amulet found underwater, and it is clearly a larger puzzle.

prose.why: The prose was atmospheric and had some good lines, such as the sad aqueduct.
